reviewer: inline (no spawn tool available; conducted by lane worker)

findings.issue: If the gate test invokes the real `node dist/cli.js`, tests break when dist is stale and become slow/flaky.
findings.resolution: Unit-test fixtures point at `process.execPath` running a trivial inline `-e` script (deterministic exit code + stdout), NOT the arbiter CLI. Shipped fixtures under __tests__/fixtures resolve the CLI path via opts.cliPath so they are not exercised by the fast unit gate.

findings.issue: Pass-rate variance for a deterministic CLI is almost always 0% or 100%, so 'variance analysis' could be vacuous.
findings.resolution: Two complementary signals: (a) outcome-stability flag (did every iteration agree?) catches genuine flakiness/regression; (b) timing percentiles (p50/p95/p99 via perf.measure) carry the continuous variance. Documented as the coherent meaning of variance for command execution.

findings.issue: A malformed scenario JSON could crash the whole run, masking other scenarios.
findings.resolution: loadScenarios narrows parsed JSON (no any), skips + records malformed fixtures as a structured error rather than throwing; mirrors loadBaseline's defensive parse in benchmark.ts.

findings.issue: Issue mentions skill BEHAVIOR; true LLM-prompt eval needs a judge model, not runnable in gated CI.
findings.resolution: Fixture schema carries a `backend` seam (cli|llm); only `cli` wired. `llm` deferred and documented. No judge model in the gate.

findings.issue: JSON.parse returns any/unknown; risk of implicit any in assertion evaluation.
findings.resolution: All parsed JSON is `unknown`, narrowed via type guards. Assertion shapes are explicit interfaces.

findings.issue: Adding a gate to check-all.mjs would require dual-sided template + dogfood.
findings.resolution: This is a dev-only self-command, NOT wired into check-all.mjs and NOT generated into target projects. Stated explicitly in plan scope section. No dual-sided burden.
